title: Stakeholder Orbit: compact QBR agenda + runner script
content:
Purpose: a compact, facilitator-friendly QBR agenda and 'runner' script that centers stakeholders using a concentric 'orbit' map, plus a one-page lightning renewal-risk radar and pre-meeting checklist. Designed for 30–60 minute executive-facing QBRs where clarity and action beats slide volume.

Use model: put this in invite as "pre-read", share the one-pager 48h before, and run the meeting from the script below. The Runner (primary facilitator) keeps time and surfaces decisions; an SRO (subject matter owner) handles product detail.

1) Pre-meeting (owner: Runner) — timeline: 48h -> 0h
- Send one-pager (this doc, status + risks + asks) 48h before.
- Confirm attendees: map using Stakeholder Orbit template (inner circle = decision-makers; middle = influencers; outer = execution/ops).
- Attach: usage trends CSV, top-3 incidents since last QBR, renewal cadence summary.
- Ask each decision-maker for 2 questions they want answered (via calendar reply) — consolidate into 'Questions queue'.
- Set clear decision asks (see 'Meeting decisions' section).

2) Agenda (45 minutes recommended)
- 0:00–0:03 — Quick open (Runner): purpose, timebox, decisions needed.
  Script: "Thanks everyone — this is a concise check-in to confirm health, unblock risks, and lock decisions required for the coming quarter. We’ll keep to 45 minutes. Our decisions today: [read Decision 1, Decision 2]. If we need more time, we’ll schedule a follow-up."
- 0:03–0:10 — Customer health snapshot (SRO): 3 slides max (adoption KPIs, latency/cost anomalies, support trends). Highlight top signal per category.
  Script: "Top-line: usage change +5% QoQ, error-rate spike defined on 2026-02-12 tied to model rollout X. What changed: [one sentence]. Impact: [one sentence]. Recommended mitigation: [one sentence]."
- 0:10–0:18 — Renewal & value recap (CS owner): usage-to-value narrative + ROI signals, highlight upsell opportunities.
  Script prompt: "Customer goals we’re supporting: [list]. Measured outcomes: [metric], [metric]. Path to expansion: [2 tactical asks]."
- 0:18–0:30 — Risk radar & mitigation (Runner leads discussion) — use the Lightning Renewal Risk Radar below. For each red/yellow item, assign owner + target date.
  Script: "We’ll run the radar quickly — call out anything in red and the single next action to de-risk it."
- 0:30–0:40 — Product alignment & roadmap handshake (Product SME): 3 items max — blockers and commitments.
  Script: "We can commit to X by date Y if we get [input/approval]."
- 0:40–0:45 — Decisions & next steps (Runner): read back decisions, owners, and dates.
  Script: "Decision 1 recorded: [text]. Owner: [name]. Due: [date]. Decision 2 recorded: ..."
- 0:45 — Close and optional 1:1 follow-ups for deep digs.

3) Stakeholder Orbit (one-page guide)
- How to map: pick 6–8 people. Draw rings: center = sponsor(s) (final approvers), inner ring = exec champions, middle ring = technical influencers, outer ring = operational owners.
- Quick cheat: color-code by renewal influence (green=high influence, amber=medium, gray=low).
- Outcome: annotate one line per person: role, decision authority (yes/no), best ask format (email/Slack/meeting).

4) Lightning Renewal Risk Radar (single page, five signals)
- Expiry timeline: <<60d / 61–120d / >120d — call out where contract sits.
- Signals (RED/AMBER/GREEN):
  1) Usage trend mismatch (sustained -15% over 30d) — data owner: usage-team. Mitigation: targeted adoption play.
  2) SLAs & latency exceptions (any P0 in last 30d) — product-owner. Mitigation: postmortem + hotfix window.
  3) Cost surprise (bill delta >+20% vs forecast) — finance + Runner. Mitigation: propose batching/quantization review with Redwood Optimize.
  4) Integration friction (open tickets >5 for core integration) — integration lead. Mitigation: dedicated fix sprint or professional services offer.
  5) Exec attention (recent escalations to VP+) — CSM + Sponsor. Mitigation: exec briefing + concrete ask.
- For each RED item capture: current state (1 sentence), impact (1 sentence), next action (owner + due date).

5) Pre-meeting checklist (Runner) — quick bullet checklist to paste into calendar invite
- Attach: one-pager PDF (this doc), usage CSV, top-3 incidents, renewal calendar export.
- Confirm attendees and timezones.
- Pre-load 'Questions queue' doc (Google doc) and share edit link.
- Prep 3 data visualizations: usage trend, tail latency P95, spend vs forecast.
- Confirm Product SME availability for roadmap handshake.

6) Facilitation tips & micro-scripts
- Interrupt politely: "Pause — we’re over time on this topic. Quick decision: accept proposed action or schedule follow-up?"
- Reframe off-track detail: "Great detail — for the group decision we need a 1-line summary: what is the one thing you need to move forward?"
- Handle turf calls: "Let’s capture the technical question here and set a 1:1 with [name] after the meeting so we don’t block the group."

7) Post-meeting artifacts & cadence
- Immediately after: Runner posts meeting notes and decisions in shared Confluence space and pings owners in Slack. Use a standard subject: "CS QBR — [Customer] — decisions & owners."
- Follow-up cadence: owner updates tracker weekly until all decisions closed.

8) Example compact tracker row (copy into sheet)
- Columns: decision_id | decision_text | owner | due_date | status | confidence | notes
- Example: D-001 | Approve 10% commit increase for Dedicated pool | Maya Thompson | 2026-03-15 | in_progress | 0.7 | awaiting finance approval

9) Meeting mateirals to attach (quick list)
- One-pager (this doc)
- Usage: last 90 days CSV + top-10 endpoints by call volume
- Incident summary: top 3 with root cause notes
- Renewal calendar export + current MRR/ARR breakdown

Open questions / TODOs
- Add templated one-pager generator (need data queries from analytics) — owner: Jordan Lee.
- Decide whether to include an "ask template" email for renewals (short ask + attachment) — owner: Priya Menon.

Notes: keep this intentionally small — the goal is to leave with decisions, not pages. If the customer asks for deeper technical dive, schedule a 30–60 minute follow-up with Product SME and Infra lead.

Last updated: 2026-02-28 by Maya Thompson.
